issues.legal_issue: A tenure holder acquired the relevant land rights only when the required certificate was granted under the law then in force, where the later amendment changing the effective date was not made retrospective.
material_facts: The tenure holder deposited the required amount to acquire the higher land rights and transferred the land on the same day.
The certificate granting those rights was issued after the transfer but before the 1962 amendment took effect.
The amendment substituted the deposit date for the certificate date, but did not make that change retrospective for this provision.
issues.conclusion: Under the law applicable to the transfer, the tenure holder acquired the higher land rights from the date the certificate was issued, not from the date of deposit.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 134 and 137 of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, as they stood before the 1962 amendment, made the rights effective from the date of the certificate. The amendment to section 137(2) changed that result but was not retrospective for this provision. The Court approved Ram Swarup v. Deputy Director, Consolidation, ILR 1971 (1) All. 698, which approved Dhani Ram v. Jokhu on the effect of the pre-amendment law.

rule.if: land_rights_acquisition_case and required_payment_made and transfer_preceded_certificate and governing_law_made_rights_effective_on_certificate and amendment_not_retroactive

predicates.land_rights_acquisition_case: The dispute concerns a tenure holder's acquisition of higher rights in land.
predicates.required_payment_made: The tenure holder made the payment required to acquire the higher land rights.
predicates.transfer_preceded_certificate: The tenure holder transferred the land before receiving the certificate granting the higher rights.
predicates.governing_law_made_rights_effective_on_c: The law applicable to the transfer made the higher rights effective upon issuance of a certificate.
predicates.amendment_not_retroactive: A later amendment changing the effective date was not made retrospective for the relevant provision.

issues.definition: When a land-rights acquisition dispute involves the required payment, a transfer before certification, and governing law that makes rights effective on certification without a retrospective amendment, the rights take effect upon certification.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee may rely on a transferor's erroneous representation of authority to transfer property when the transferor subsequently acquires the interest represented, provided the transferee acted on the representation and did not know it was false.
material_facts: The transferor executed a sale deed for consideration on the same day he deposited the amount required to acquire higher rights in the land.
At the time of the sale, the transferor had not yet received the certificate granting those rights; he received it afterward.
The circumstances showed that the transferor represented that he was authorized to transfer the property and that the vendee acted on that representation.
The challengers did not claim to be transferees in good faith, and the Court found no basis to conclude that the vendee knew the transferor lacked the represented title.
issues.conclusion: Section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act applied, so the transferor's subsequently acquired title enured to the vendee and the challenge to the sale failed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 43 of the Transfer of Property Act embodies an estoppel: a transferor who fraudulently or erroneously represents authority to transfer property cannot deny that representation against a transferee who acted on it, once the transferor subsequently acquires the represented interest. The transferor's good or bad faith is immaterial; the transferee's reliance is material, and section 43 does not assist a transferee who knew the transferor lacked the represented title. Section 6(a) addresses a different subject and does not displace section 43. The Court relied on Jumma Masjid v. Kodimaniandra Deviah, AIR 1962 SC 847, and approved the reasoning in Ram Swarup v. Deputy Director, Consolidation, ILR 1971 (1) All. 698; it also discussed Official Assignee, Madras v. Sanpath Naidu, 65 Mad LJ 588.

rule.if: property_transfer_dispute and transferor_represented_authority_to_transfer and transfer_made_for_consideration and transferor_later_acquired_represented_interest and transferee_acted_on_representation and not transferee_knew_representation_was_false

predicates.property_transfer_dispute: The dispute concerns a transfer of property by a person claiming authority to transfer it.
predicates.transferor_represented_authority_to_tran: The transferor represented that they had authority to transfer the property.
predicates.transfer_made_for_consideration: The transferor purported to transfer the property for consideration.
predicates.transferor_later_acquired_represented_in: The transferor subsequently acquired the interest they had represented themselves as having.
predicates.transferee_acted_on_representation: The transferee relied on the transferor's representation when taking the transfer.
predicates.transferee_knew_representation_was_false: The transferee knew, when taking the transfer, that the transferor lacked the represented interest or authority.

issues.definition: When a property transfer for consideration follows a representation of authority, the transferor later acquires the represented interest, and the transferee relied on the representation without knowing it was false, that later-acquired interest enures to the transferee.
